is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.l., including An. gambiae s.s. (S and M forms) and An. arabiensis (Page 1, Abstract; Page 2, Methods).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports the frequency of the Vgsc L1014F (kdr) mutation (Page 2, Page 4).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper reports the frequency of the 1014F allele in a sub-sample of S-form An. gambiae s.s. (95.8% in both test and control samples, N=12 for each test) (Page 4).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from the villages of Soumousso and Laye in south-west Burkina Faso (Page 2, Page 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research study reporting original experimental data on mosquito age and insecticide resistance.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data are tied to specific villages: Soumousso (N 11° 00’ 46”, W 04° 03’ 25”) and Laye (N 12° 31’ 35”, W 1° 46’ 21”) (Page 2, Page 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were conducted between August and November 2010 (Page 2, Page 3).

duplicate_risk.evidence: While the study mentions routine monitoring as part of a WHO/TDR multi-country project (Page 2), the specific data on aging and the 2010 collections appear to be unique to this publication.

supplement.evidence: The necessary genotype frequency and sample size are provided in the main text (Page 4). Additional File 1 contains statistical model details rather than raw genotype counts.

assessment.summary: This study investigates how mosquito age affects insecticide susceptibility in Anopheles gambiae s.l. populations from Burkina Faso. It reports that older mosquitoes (17-19 days) are significantly more susceptible to deltamethrin and bendiocarb than younger mosquitoes (3-5 days). The study provides the frequency of the Vgsc L1014F mutation in An. gambiae s.s. (S-form) and compares frequencies between deltamethrin-exposed (dead) and control mosquitoes.
